note: Landenmark et al. 2015: 5.3e+37 +/- 3.6e+37 letters; census 1.80e+37 letters sits at the low end

303 million distinct genes already sampled at 95% identity (Coelho et al. 2022) x 1,000 letters x 2 bits. The census's 3.8x10^12 bits implies about 1.9 billion distinct genes, about 6 times the sampled catalogue; plausible because sampling is far from complete (Locey & Lennon 2016 PNAS 113:5970 estimate about 10^12 microbial species).
85% for microbes matches gene-dense microbial genomes; 15% for complex cells sits between humans (about 8%) and flies, worms and yeast (18-68%).
